newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME nickel seen dipping on Inco strike deal - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel seen dipping on Inco strike deal - trade.

text.p: Nickel prices are tipped to open lower and test the $7,000 level on the London Metal Exchange (LME) later on Friday after news union officials had recommended a new labour deal to striking Inco metal workers.
Canada's Inco Ltd said on Thursday union negotiators for the 4,670 striking nickel workers at its Sudbury, Ontario mine would recommend a new contract deal to end a four-week strike.
An unidentified spokesman at Local 6500 of the United Steelworkers of America told Reuters that the union expected to hold a ratification vote on the deal on Saturday.
"The latest development says the miners are about to end their strike soon and that should send nickel to test $7,000 support today," a dealer for a metal firm in Singapore said.
But dealers said expectations of the end of the industrial action had already been largely factored into the nickel price and they believed the metal's downside would be limited.
Three-month nickel was indicated at $7,070 a tonne on the LME on Thursday, up $20 from Wednesday.
"There is not much room for nickel to fall," one trader said. "It may test $6,900 support after the strike ends."
Dealers said LME three-month copper was quoted around $2,410 a tonne at 0545 GMT in Asian trade on Friday compared with a late indication in London on Thursday of $2,398.
They said the red metal was finding some support from being slightly oversold and should consolidate around $2,400 before the market finds fresh direction.
LME broker Rudolph Wolff pegged copper's support lower between $2,245 to $2,350 with a initial target at $2,350 in its daily report.
Wolff also said reports of worsening weather conditions in South America had caused some concern over near-term supply tightness within the market.
Far East dealers said aluminium is expected to trade in a narrow range on the LME later on Friday due to the absence of new market-moving factors.
One aluminium dealer pegged the trading range for three-month metal between $1,570 to $1,580.
